commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[rl] Refresh inventory-only declarations at catalog publication (#11167)

Catalog publication now takes the current code declaration for a source
that has no pipeline and no attempt in the campaign. Previously every
source without an attempt carried its prior snapshot row forward
unchanged. An inventory-only source can never have an attempt, so an
edit
to its declaration never reached production.

The five Smartie campaign releases show this. #10924 added their
`independent_qc`, but the production catalog still serves the
declarations published on Nov 4, so the Atlas Independent QC column is
empty for them. A local catalog reproduces it: a second publication with
the edited declaration kept `independent_qc` empty. The new test covers
that case.

Runnable sources keep their prior declaration when unselected, because
their grade is pinned to the declaration it assessed. The refresh also
requires that the prior row had no pipeline, so a source that loses its
pipeline in code keeps its graded row.

After merge, one FULL campaign on
`snowball-v01-structure-closure-validation`
with `--publish-catalog` and an Atlas loader run will bring the five
releases' QC into the Atlas.

Co-authored-by: Ben Feuer <benfeuer@Bens-MacBook-Pro.local>

commits.author: mminutoli
commits.message:
[grug] Let the June synthetic benchmark repeat a pool of batches (#11140)

The June synthetic benchmark gives every step fresh uniform-random
tokens, so the loss stays at ln(vocab_size) and run-to-run differences
near that floor are noise. `--repeat-batches N` draws the sequences from
a pool of N batches that the mixture's restart strategy cycles through,
so the model can memorize the pool, the loss falls, and two
configurations' loss curves can be compared. The default, 0, keeps fresh
tokens every step.

The dataset holds only the pool, so long runs are not limited by
MixtureDataset's 2^16-sequence block cap (127 steps at batch 512 with
fresh tokens); a pool of 2^16 or more sequences still hits it, and the
benchmark now rejects it up front. We used it to compare kernel options
over 600 steps on 2 MI355X nodes: the loss falls from 11.79 to about
1e-4.

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[levanter] Make the Snowball MoE capacity a setting and count drops (#10685)

Make `SnowballConfig.moe_capacity_factor` a checked runtime setting, and
add a Snowball forward that counts dropped MoE assignments. The factor
must be positive. At the expert-axis size it keeps every routed
assignment. HF metadata does not carry it, so `train_lm` now keeps the
requested value across `use_hf_model_config`. June's training config
raises when it is set, like `router_dot_fp32`.

`SnowballLMHeadModel.activations_with_stats` takes a boolean
`token_valid` mask over the token axes. It returns the hidden states and
a `MoeForwardStats` with the routes and the per-layer sender and
receiver drop counts. Invalid positions, such as padding, are skipped
and are not counted as drops. The counts are per call, so callers sum
them across microbatches. Forwards without `token_valid` call the expert
MLP as before.

The ordinary training forward passes no validity mask, so padding uses
capacity there. Zero drops in the stats forward prove that training
dropped nothing only at dropless capacity or on a batch with no padding.

The first full parity gate failed 21 checks. Levanter's expert choices
matched the torch reference at only 41.5% of positions, and the gap grew
with depth. Levanter's expert-parallel ring used capacity 1.0 and
dropped overflow assignments without a report. vLLM never drops. On the
real model the [drop
diagnostic](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-diag-moe-drops-r2-reading-chukar-md)
measured drops of 8–23% of assignments per layer. With no drops
(capacity 4.0), the p99 log-prob gap against vLLM fell from 2–4 nats to
0.45–0.65, and route agreement rose from 0.42 to 0.89.

Part of #10695

---------

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[levanter] Add a Snowball route observer and FP32 router dot (#10684)

Add two opt-in options to the Snowball forward.
`SnowballLMHeadModel.activations_with_routes` returns the activations
and each layer's selected expert ids, shape `[L, B, S, K]`. The ids come
from the forward as it runs; routing is not recomputed.
`SnowballConfig.router_dot_fp32` casts the router input and weight to
float32 before the router dot. It changes neither parameter storage nor
HF metadata. Both are off by default, and then the forward is unchanged.

The marin vLLM fork (`01911be3`, `grugmoe.py:596,713`) keeps the router
projection in float32 and casts the input to float32 before the router
dot. Levanter did this dot in bfloat16. In a torch test on the gate's
inputs, moving the dot to float32 changed about 3,900 expert choices.
The route observer lets the identity experiments compare Levanter's
expert choices with a torch reference, layer by layer ([amendment
G1](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-precision-preflight-amendment-g1-shoveler-md)).

With `router_dot_fp32`, `train_lm` refuses to start unless
`trainer.field_dtype_overrides` maps `router_bias` to `float32`, so the
router bias also stays float32. HF metadata carries neither
`router_dot_fp32` nor `moe_implementation`. After `use_hf_model_config`
reloads the architecture, `train_lm` now copies both from the requested
config. It also keeps the requested `reference_checkpoint` and
`tokenizer`, which the reload used to reset. Non-Snowball configs reload
as before.

Packed document masks change in two ways. Query segment ids follow the
token sharding over batch and context. Key segment ids are sharded over
batch only, so every context shard sees the full key sequence. A
`key_position` axis on the key ids must have the length of the input
position axis, or the forward raises.

`JuneSnowballConfig.training_config` now passes only the fields that
June's `GrugModelConfig` has. A Snowball-only setting such as
`router_dot_fp32` raises when set, since June's kernels do not implement
it. Without this, the new field broke `GrugModelConfig(**fields)`.

Part of #10695

---------

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[levanter] Keep named fields at a configured dtype through HF export (#10683)

Add `TrainerConfig.field_dtype_overrides`, a map from a model attribute
name to the floating `jnp.dtype` that field keeps under the
mixed-precision policy. A name matches that attribute at any depth, so
`{router_bias: float32}` in YAML covers every layer. An unknown dtype
name fails when the config is decoded, and a non-floating dtype raises
when the trainer state is built. The default is empty. Then `Trainer.mp`
returns `mp` unchanged.

Snowball stores its 26 router biases in float32, and vLLM routes with
them in float32. Levanter rounded them to bfloat16 twice: when it stored
frozen parameters in the compute dtype, and when it cast the model for
the loss. The fine-tuned model therefore routed with different biases
from the served model. The [block-0 dtype
comparison](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-l0-dtype-boundaries-marten-md)
lists each router operand on both sides.

With overrides set, `Trainer.mp` is a `jmp.Policy` subclass whose param
and compute casts give each overridden field its own dtype. Code that
uses the trainer's policy follows it: the training and eval loss,
labeled evaluation, and the eval-harness and logit paths in `train_lm`.
HF load in `train_lm` and in the DPO policy and reference loads reads
tensors at their stored dtype before the param cast. HF export,
including the DPO export, writes each overridden field in its own dtype
when the rest of the model is saved in bfloat16. `lora_lm` loads its
base the same way, and its merged export, the LoRA adaptor's merged
export and `export_lm_to_hf` pass the overrides too. An overridden name
that matches no floating-point array raises when the trainer state is
built.

The new `frozen_parameters` adaptor trains every field except the named
ones and exports the full model. Its checkpoints omit the frozen fields,
so a resume must load them from the same pinned base.

Part of #10695

---------

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[finelog] Raise the default query deadline to 30 seconds (#11087)

Raise the server's default Query and FetchLogs deadline from 10 to 30
seconds. The `finelog query` CLI now waits 35 seconds by default, so it
still outlasts the server and reports the server's error instead of a
bare
client timeout.

Day-sized log scans on the `marin` hub do not fit in 10 seconds. A
60-day
pull of `levanter.model_cache` lines in 12-hour windows lost 58% of its
windows to `snapshot read deadline exceeded`, even after three retries
per
window (see #9233).

The 10-second value came from #7312 and #8010, which bounded runaway
scans
that held the visibility lock and delayed compaction. #10929 removed the
cache visibility contention. The server still caps each read at the
earliest
of this default, the caller's Connect deadline, and the table's
`max_query_time_ms`. The Grafana bridge sends a 20-second deadline, so
dashboard reads keep their current bound. Admission still allows two
concurrent Query RPCs, so a slow ad-hoc query without a deadline can now
hold
a slot for up to 30 seconds.

The new default takes effect when the hub is redeployed.

Part of #9233

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[sft] Keep only the final native checkpoint by default (#10782)

Chat SFT now keeps one rolling native recovery checkpoint and saves a
permanent native checkpoint only when training finishes. The recovery
checkpoint is saved every 30 minutes and holds the full training state,
including optimizer state and the step counter. Before this change,
Levanter SFT kept a permanent checkpoint every 5,000 steps, and the
two-stage Grug recipe kept one every 1,000 steps.

`SFTSpec` now has a `checkpointer` field, a Levanter
`CheckpointerConfig`, and both the Levanter and native Grug backends use
it. Set `keep` to retain intermediate permanent checkpoints. Set
`keep_last_temporary_checkpoints` to change how many recovery copies
remain. The Grug `save_interval_minutes` and `checkpoint_keep` options
are removed. The Grug smoke run sets `keep` so that it still exercises a
mid-run save.

Recovery checkpoints go under Marin's TTL scratch prefix, where cloud
stores expire objects after 14 days. Automatic resume searches both the
temporary and the permanent roots. After the final native save commits,
the remaining temporary checkpoints are removed. The Levanter backend
still writes its final HF export.

A Snowball native checkpoint takes hundreds of GiB, and the identity
runs share the cw-rno2a storage quota. On 2026-10-29 the bucket filled
and was write-suspended. Running exports sat idle on their GPUs until
space was freed.

Part of #10695

---------

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: ravwojdyla
commits.message:
[grug] Count MoE routing assignments in int32 (#11166)

`moe_routing_stats` and `moe_routing_stats_local` now count each
expert's assignments in int32. They used a float32 one-hot reduced in
float32, and float32 holds integers exactly only up to 2**24, about
16.8M.

On 11 hero racks, a layer makes 176 x 262,144 x 8 = 369M assignments, a
mean of about 961K per expert. With the router bias frozen for SFT, hot
experts take 15-35 times the mean, so their counts round. The valid
count then misses the batch size. The trainer's drop-metric check
(`valid plus skipped assignments must equal the padded batch size`)
stopped the first production SFT attempt at its first step ([run
record](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8089#issuecomment-6761658823)).
One-rack runs and pretraining, where the bias kept experts near the
mean, stayed below 2**24.

The largest global count, 369M, fits in int32. Fractions, entropy and
the load-balancing loss still divide in float32, so training is
unchanged. The new test routes 2**24 + 1 assignments to one expert;
without the change it reads 16,777,216.

Part of #8089

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
Remove unsupported Harbor agents from vendored runtime (#11080)

Marin can launch only six Harbor agents. Vendored Harbor still included
unsupported agent implementations, simulated-user bridges, and an AIME
smoke policy that selected a removed agent. Those paths could pass
configuration parsing and fail later during evaluation.

Limit the vendored runtime to Pi, Mini-SWE-Agent, Codex, OpenCode,
Terminus-2, and Terminus-Kira, selected by name. Delete the unsupported
agents, the bridge and local-mode runtimes, simulated-user configuration
and CLI options, the agent `import_path` and `mode` fields, and their
tests. Remove the obsolete AIME smoke policy, the SOTOPIA cohort job
field, and the Tau3 Pi and ACP image recipe.

Every job and trial must select a supported agent, which the agent
factory checks before construction. Unknown config fields are rejected
where a policy enters: Marin preflight and Harbor's `jobs start` and
`trials start` config files. The stored `JobConfig` and `TrialConfig`
models still ignore unknown fields, so job directories written before
this change, which carry null `user_agent` and `sotopia_cohort` fields,
can still be resumed and read.

Marin preflight validates the selected agent and environment before
submission. The trial driver resolves the agent class once and applies
agent-specific settings from it. An offline test checks every active
Harbor policy without downloading remote datasets. The integration
preflight still exercises a representative policy. Documentation uses
the supported AIME policy with a task limit.

The September 24 verified policy keeps its `tau3-pi` and `sotopia-hard`
entries so recorded results still validate against it. Their campaign
configs remain as records and fail preflight if relaunched. Archived
SOTOPIA score readers remain available for past results. The
process-reaping work remains in #10735, which is stacked on this PR.

---------

Co-authored-by: Ben Feuer <benfeuer@Bens-MacBook-Pro.local>
Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[skyrl] Apply task-scoped Harbor trial policy (#10845)

Original Harbor tasks can need different resource limits, MCP servers,
and verifier environment values. SkyRL's
`InstalledAgentRuntime.run_original_trial` did not apply these settings
by task ID. `RolloutEngine` could also apply the agent deadline to the
complete Harbor trial. This could stop the trial before Harbor finished
verification.

Select a task binding by canonical task ID. Apply its resource
overrides, agent MCP servers, and literal verifier environment values to
the original trial. For original Harbor trials, clear
`model_turn_timeout`, `tool_turn_timeout`, and `total_turn_timeout` on
the `RolloutEngine` task specification. Harbor keeps the agent and
verifier phase deadlines. `RolloutEngine` keeps the full-attempt
deadline so verification can finish after the agent phase ends.

Shellbox Daytona prepares the task image. Selecting a saved snapshot by
name and expanding host variables in verifier settings need separate
backend support.

---------

Co-authored-by: Benjamin Feuer <penfever@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Ben Feuer <benfeuer@Bens-MacBook-Pro.local>

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[evaldash] Show a run's declared metrics ahead of the raw map (#10971)

Run pages now lead with the benchmark's declared protocol metrics and
keep the evaluator's raw metric map in a collapsed "All raw metrics (N)"
section. The run payload resolves the declared rows through the
evaluation adapter, so task directories match as the statistics engine
matches them, values come from canonical_metrics, and a missing
canonical value falls back to the raw source metric under the same
extraction-filter priority (`flexible-extract` first) that ranking uses.
The primary metric leads each task. Tasks without benchmark metadata
keep their raw rows in the top table, and records that declare no
benchmark protocol show the raw table unchanged.

The NUPA5K-Loose record for this run declares accuracy, digit_match, and
format_valid_rate but stores 1,125 raw keys: base metrics, four length
buckets, and a per-task bucket for every operator. The page rendered all
of them as top-level rows and never showed the declared accuracy name.

The run's zero accuracy and all-incorrect samples are the stored
policy-scorer result, not a display defect. Under the strict NUPA rule
from #10876, Snowball and Grug NUPA cells score near 0 unless they are
served with think markers preserved (`skip_special_tokens: false`, or
the `grug` reasoning parser); the #10197 discussion covers the serving
setting. EvalDash reads the recorded per-item zeros unchanged.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Export hero log scaling at artifact schema 3 (#11128)

The hero model multiplies each query in its global-attention layers by
`(1 + 0.1 · ln(max(n / 65536, 1)))²`, where `n` is the query's position
in its document. The factor is 1 up to position 65,536 and 1.296 at
position 262,144. The current hero checkpoint,
`hero-lce-log65536sq-step390k`, trained with this factor (#10923,
#10986).

Before this change, `GrugModelConfig.to_hf_config` raised an error for a
config with this "log scaling". Thus we could not export the checkpoint
to Hugging Face format or upload it.

This change raises `grugmoe_artifact_schema_version` to 3 for every hero
export. It always writes the three settings (`log_scaling_n_floor`,
`log_scaling_alpha`, `log_scaling_power`) to `config.json`, as null when
log scaling is off. `from_hf_config` reads them back, and treats them as
off when they are absent from a schema-1 or schema-2 artifact. Exports
already written keep their schema-2 `config.json`. `upload_hf` and an
interrupted export compare against the config that the current code
builds, so upload or resume an older export with the exporter revision
that wrote it.

Schema 3 prevents a silent error. The current vLLM and SkyRL Grug models
ignore unknown config keys and apply only a fixed scale per layer. But
they reject a schema other than 1 or 2. Thus they refuse every new hero
export, with or without log scaling, until they support schema 3, and
never run a log-scaled export with the wrong attention scale after
position 65,536.

Serving needs a change to our vLLM fork and a new wheel pin. RL needs a
SkyRL change. #11127 tracks both.

Part of #11127

commits.author: ravwojdyla
commits.message:
[grug] Default the hero SFT capacity factor to 1.625 (#11164)

`--capacity-factor` in `launch_hero_sft.py` now defaults to 1.625
instead of being required. At CP4 x EP16 with the default remat slop,
1.625 is the highest routed capacity factor that fits. At 1.6875 the
first all-to-all runs out of HBM, and at 1.75 and 2.0 the
rematerialization check fails during compile.

With the router bias frozen, a one-rack, 100-update run from step-393491
drops 3.60% of expert assignments at 1.625 and 0.56% with the
step-393491 expert placement. Peak memory and step time match capacity
factor 1.5. The sweep and the runs are in the [#8089 plan
comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8089#issuecomment-6760446807).

Part of #8089

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Balance hero SFT expert load with a static expert placement (#11149)

With a frozen router bias, SFT data sends most load to a few hot
experts, and the ragged all-to-all drops tokens at their capacity
blocks. This change renumbers the routed experts of each layer, so that
each capacity block gets a similar load.

- The smoke run `hero-sft-smoke-v2` (frozen bias, capacity factor 1.5,
CP4 x EP16, one rack) dropped 5.0% of routed assignments. Pretraining on
the same mesh dropped about 3e-4.
- `expert_placement.py` builds a placement from the per-expert routing
histograms of a W&B run, by greedy longest-processing-time. The
`--expert-placement` launcher option reads it.
- The trainer applies the placement one time, when it restores the
source checkpoint of the placement. It moves the router columns, router
bias, pending QB betas, expert weights, and their optimizer state
together. The model computes the same function.
- The trainer does not apply the placement again to checkpoints of the
run, which the launcher writes below `expert-placement-<fingerprint>/`.
- Weight merging against the pretraining checkpoint must apply
`ExpertPlacement.inverse()` first.
- The Levanter change only moves `capacity_block_experts()` into a
function.
- One-rack test, 26 steps, same data and start checkpoint as v2:

| Metric | v2 | Placed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Drops | 5.0% | 0.77% |
| Mean loss | 0.5831 | 0.5757, lower at each shared step |
| s/step (median) | 23.9 | 23.5 |
| Peak HBM | 130.77 GiB | 130.77 GiB |

- At step 0, before any update, the loss was 3.45% lower, so the drops
alone cost about 3.5% loss.
- Measured drops agreed with the histogram projection to within 0.0005
per step. The placement took 13 s.
- The test is in-sample: the placement came from the same 25 v2 steps.
With held-out steps, a placement from 5 steps projects 0.71% at capacity
factor 1.5.

Part of #8089

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[evaldash] Open links without a cohort on the newest scores (#11133)

A link without `?cohort=` now opens on the newest admissible result per
benchmark across cohorts, shown with the mixed-settings warning. Before,
a missing cohort meant `eval-policy-2026-09-24-verified`. The Panel,
Compare and model pages also wrote that default into the URL.

Links posted before the cohort was part of the URL, and every run of the
2026-10-16 policy, therefore opened on an empty view. Those runs carry
no version label, and no verified cohort exists for that policy.
Examples are the compare and model links in #10695, #9920, #9984 and
#10213.

For existing links:

| Link | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| no `cohort` | 09-24 cohort, often empty | newest per benchmark, all
cohorts, with the warning |
| `cohort=<label>` | that cohort | that cohort (unchanged) |
| `cohort=eval-policy-2026-09-24-verified` written in by the old default
| 09-24 cohort | 09-24 cohort (unchanged; switch the selector to see
current runs) |

`/meta` reports `default_cohort: "all"`. The Panel drops its separate
"Default" entry, which is now the same as "all cohorts". The change
takes effect when EvalDash is next released.

Stacked on #11132. Fixes #11089

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[evaldash] Select unversioned runs as their own cohort (#11132)

Runs launched without a version label (`version: null`) are now a cohort
of their own, selected with `cohort=unversioned` on the Panel, Compare
and model views. The cohort selector lists it whenever such runs exist,
with a warning that they have no settings contract.

Before, the selector listed only named versions, and the API read a null
`cohort_version` as "all cohorts". The runs of the current eval policy,
launched from the campaign script without `--version`, could therefore
be reached only through the all-cohorts view. Selection now reads the
cohort mode (`latest_valid` or `single_cohort`), so a single cohort can
be the null version.

`panel_request` takes the `cohort` query value (`all`, `unversioned` or
a version label) instead of `cohort_version`. The model and run pages
already linked to `?cohort=unversioned`. Those links now resolve the
same way on the Panel and Compare.

Stacked on #11131. Part of #11089

commits.author: karansag
commits.message:
[evaldash] Compare models across cohorts behind the mixed-settings warning (#11131)

Compare now answers for every cohort selection, including "Newest per
benchmark (all cohorts)". Before, `/compare` answered that selection
with a 400, and the Panel and Compare pages disabled model selection.
Runs without a version label could only be reached through that
selection, so they could never be compared.

The existing warning that all cohorts may mix evaluation settings stays
on the Panel and on Compare. A comparison across cohorts can rest on
runs with different settings, and the reader is told so. Each cell still
names the cohort it came from.

Existing links are unchanged: a link that names a cohort compares within
it, as before. This is the first of three stacked changes for #11089.
The next two add a cohort for unversioned runs and change what a link
without `?cohort=` opens on.

commits.message:
[grug] Add full-model SFT for the hero on the 10.05 mix (#11136)

Add `launch_hero_sft.py`, which continues a hero checkpoint on the SFT
recipe of `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05`. The
recipe has five parts:

- one packed epoch of the 216 full A/B stores in complete mixture
blocks;
- about 20% replay from the hero's 262K Harrier mix;
- the resumed pretraining optimizer with SFT learning rates;
- the seven chat-token LM-head reseeds;
- a √32 learning-rate scale on those rows.

The store manifest points at the CoreWeave copies in the hero's region.
The hero trainer gains a router-bias mode and the special-token reseed
with its update scale; the defaults leave pretraining unchanged.
`LmDataConfig.mixture_start_step` now accepts multi-stage mixtures and
counts their stage steps from that step, so the SFT epoch starts at its
first sequence on the restored step.

10.05 froze the router bias. It trained with expert axis 1, where
`capacity_overflow_rate_mean` is 0. The hero runs EP16 at capacity
factor 1.5. On one hero rack from step-393491, 20 updates with a frozen
bias dropped 5.8–8.1% of expert assignments; with the bias updating,
drops stayed near 3e-5. The frozen bias had lower loss over those 20
updates: 0.646 against 0.698 train loss on the same batch, and 1.712
against 1.742 dropless Paloma eval loss. `--router-bias` defaults to
`frozen`, as in 10.05, and `--capacity-factor` is required. A frozen
bias at capacity factor 2.0 fails XLA compilation of the train step.

The one-rack smoke tests
([frozen](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-smoke-v2),
[updating](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/runs/hero-sft-smoke-v3-update))
ran on the pre-merge head of #11044, which computes the same model as
main. Each restored step-393491 and reseeded the special-token columns
on all 64 ranks. Each trained at 23 s per step with the pretraining peak
memory of 130.77 GiB. The frozen run saved its checkpoint and resumed
from it without a second reseed. Export and serving still refuse log
scaling (#11056 B5).

[grug] Apply fa4_bounds windows in reference attention (#11135)

Reference attention now applies the per-query key lower bounds carried
in `AttentionMask.fa4_bounds`, so it keeps only keys at or after each
query's bound.

Grug models that scan their layers (`moe_hero_ep`, `moe_hero_fsdp`,
`moe_hero_pipeline`, `fast_track`) cannot vary the static
`sliding_window` field inside the scan. They pass every layer a
full-causal mask and carry each layer's window only in `fa4_bounds`,
through `with_fa4_bounds`. `materialize_mask` ignored those bounds, so
on the reference path, which `attention()` uses by default on CPU and
any non-TPU backend, the Hero's local layers attended to every earlier
token instead of the last 2,048. The FA4 and AMD Triton kernels already
read the bounds, so production GPU training and evaluation are
unchanged.

This surfaced while checking SkyRL's Megatron Grug model against a tiny
JAX Hero oracle. Megatron diverged from the oracle at exactly position
16, the window. With this fix, the two agree to bf16 noise at every
probed layer (logits 0.58% relative).

Existing Hero CPU tests compare variants run on the same path, so they
pass before and after this change. The new tests fail without the fix.
TPU splash and `xla_flash` also ignore `fa4_bounds`; no Grug model
selects them for these variants today.

Part of #11127

[loom] Replace the gdoc profile with a Loom artifact doc profile (#11060)

Add a `doc` Loom profile whose record of the work is the branch artifact
`doc`, and remove the `gdoc` profile and its Google Doc tool. People
read the doc in the session, comment on selected text, and edit its
source. The agent keeps the doc current and posts progress updates to
the artifact `progress`.

The profile sets `docArtifact: doc`, which marin-community/loom#421
adds. With it, Loom opens the session on a Doc tab that shows `doc`, and
sends the agent a message that starts with "A person edited the doc"
when a person saves an edit. The instructions describe that behavior,
and Loom ignores the setting until the change is deployed, so merge this
PR after marin-community/loom#421 is rolled out to loom.oa.dev.

The instructions keep the Gates section directly below the Objective.
They tell the agent that a single comment arrives as soon as the person
writes it, and that it continues the work a review stopped.

The Docs API stays enabled for the pm profile's goals doc. The Drive API
leaves the Pulumi stack because only the gdoc tool used it; with
`disable_on_destroy=False`, it stays enabled in the project.
